design_evaluation.summary: A polished dark/light dual-theme site with a strong hero, clear nav, and functional mobile menu, login modal, and consent-gated chat panel. Hierarchy and interaction patterns are generally solid, but floating widgets overlap content, some secondary text has low contrast, and accessibility affordances (focus states, semantic cues) are not evidenced in the screenshots.
strengths: Hero headline uses a clear two-tier emphasis ('AI Testing & Integration.' white / 'Building Trust.' gradient) with supporting stats and dual CTAs (Live Feed, AI Lab) — strong visual hierarchy on ui-home-desktop
Theme toggle fully restyles the UI consistently (dark to light) without breaking component structure, as shown in ui-theme-toggle
Login modal (ui-login-modal) uses a proper overlay with dimmed/blurred background, clear Login/Register tabs, labeled fields, primary CTA, and a visible close (X) control
Chat panel (ui-chat-opens) includes a consent gate with disclaimer text, checkbox, terms link, and a visibly disabled 'Agree & Start Chat' button until consent — good interaction clarity
Mobile menu (ui-mobile-menu) presents all nav items plus 'Break it' at full-width touch targets with a clear close button
Feature cards use distinct accent colors with consistent structure (icon, title, description, action link) across all screenshots
issues: The floating 'Voice Agent' pill and chat bubble overlap the fourth feature card's description text on both desktop and mobile, obscuring content ('Reliability & Fact Check' card in ui-home-desktop; 'Adversarial Simulation' card in ui-mobile-menu)
Muted secondary text (card descriptions, stat labels like 'ARTICLES TODAY') has low contrast against dark backgrounds, risking WCAG AA failure
No visible focus indicators or aria/state cues can be confirmed in any screenshot; accessibility_cues are weak beyond icon presence
Mobile header (ui-mobile-menu) crowds the gear and Login buttons next to the close icon at narrow width — tight touch-target spacing
The chat panel in ui-chat-opens shows large empty space above and below the consent block; content should be vertically centered or the panel sized to content
The 'LIVE' vertical tab is clipped flush to the left edge with the dot overlapping its edge; its purpose and clickability are unclear
Color-coded card action links (red/purple/green/orange 'Explore/Scan/Verify/Check') rely on color alone to differentiate; labels carry the meaning but the red 'Explore' can read as an error state

candidate_findings.title: article-proxy-ssrf-loopback-rejection
candidate_findings.expected: Response is a controlled 4xx JSON error (e.g., blocked_url / invalid url); body must not leak stack traces, internal paths, or upstream fetch content
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF guard itself behaved correctly in substance: the loopback URL http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin was not fetched (image/title are null, error message explicitly cites 'private/internal IP 127.0.0.1'), the response was parseable JSON with no stack traces, internal paths, upstream content, or sensitive markers, and no HTTP 500 occurred. However, the stated contract expected a controlled 4xx status (400/403/422), and the server returned HTTP 200 with the rejection encoded in the body ('error' key). This is an error-signaled-as-success pattern: the semantic security intent was met, but the documented status-code contract was violated, so the positive expectation is not fully supported.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
